gaps.gap: Time to first job and school-to-work transition
gaps.why: The project question is how graduates move into work. No source here measures it.
gaps.have: Only passing mention of school-to-work transition in the 2018-19 CAS report.
gaps.next: Specify a graduate tracer pilot with a partner university (AUB proposed) to record time to first job and employment by programme.

gaps.why: Youth (15-24) unemployment includes people who are not graduates and misses graduates older than 24.
gaps.have: Youth unemployment series; one 'advanced education' value for Lebanon in the 2015-21 World Bank table (about 14.5%, year not shown).
gaps.next: Extract unemployment by education level from the 2018-19 report (Figure 3.18) and the Jan 2022 tables; state clearly that it is not a graduate rate.

gaps.why: The 2022 numbers (29.6%, 47.8%, NEET, informality) are the headline post-crisis figures but currently come from a Blom Invest Bank blog.
gaps.next: Download the tables from the CAS January 2022 survey page, or the ILO report, and confirm each value.

gaps.gap: Modelled and survey estimates diverge after 2019
gaps.why: WDI modelled unemployment stays near 11% in 2022 while the survey reports 29.6%. Trend charts built only on WDI would understate the shock.
gaps.next: Show survey points separately from the modelled line and label both clearly.

gaps.why: Only 2018-19 (and a single 2015-21 snapshot) exist, so no 2008-2023 trend by education level.
gaps.next: Load the snapshot and the report's education breakdown into this file as separate, labelled survey points.

gaps.why: NEET shows how many young people are neither studying nor working.
gaps.have: Two survey points (2018-19 and Jan 2022) by sex; no WDI series in the panel.
gaps.next: Pull the WDI NEET series (SL.UEM.NEET.ZS) for Lebanon and comparators and check coverage.

gaps.why: The plan is to show 2024 where available.
gaps.have: In WDI, 2024 has only net migration and education spending; unemployment, participation and enrolment stop at 2023.
gaps.next: Recheck WDI after its next update; keep 2024 separate.

gaps.why: Some context variables have too few points for trends.
gaps.have: Lebanon has only 3 migrant stock observations and 6 for tertiary spending per student; Egypt has 1 education spending value.
gaps.next: Avoid trend charts for these, or drop them.

gaps.why: Arab Barometer measures wishes to emigrate, not people leaving.
gaps.have: Net migration (UN estimate) plus survey intentions.
gaps.next: Keep intentions and net migration in separate charts; look for departure data from official sources.

gaps.why: We know intention by education and age, but not for graduates who are unemployed or underemployed.
gaps.next: Arab Barometer microdata (Wave VIII) could give this crosstab; confirm permission and scope.

gaps.why: Career-services teams plan by institution and programme.
